scope: Apply the adapter's raw-section count, group and retained-byte limits at the low-level DXF setter, adoption and replay boundaries.

behavior: Const-section staging estimates the complete nested value payload before copying, stages into a temporary vector, and swaps only after a successful copy; rejection or allocation failure clears stale sections and leaves a sticky input-rejection state.
Rvalue setter and adoption paths estimate before moving; rejected input remains owned by the caller and stale codec sections are discarded.
A valid replacement clears the rejection state. The next write refuses a pending rejected setter before opening its output transaction.
The aggregate section/group/byte budget is rechecked at the raw replay boundary, and direct single-section writes enforce the same per-section logical-byte ceiling.
Adapter capture now aliases the same shared constants, preventing resource ceilings from drifting between capture and serialization.

normalFocused.coverage: Exact/under byte-bound estimator behavior; over-count const/move/adopt refusal; caller ownership preservation; valid adoption/return; ASCII/Binary destination preservation after rejected setter input; corrected same-codec output retry; existing adapter capture limit.

limitations: The byte estimate bounds logical owned values, not vector/string capacity, allocator overhead or process RSS.
These internal ceilings are resource limits, not DXF format maxima or support claims.
The allocation-failure branch of const-vector staging was not fault-injected in this slice.
A private dxfRW state field changed class layout; downstream consumers must rebuild, and ABI compatibility remains an open P8 gate.
The transport and rollback controls do not qualify physical producer coverage or native consumer semantics.
next: Continue the P6 safety and caller-state audit on other unbounded copy, assembly, allocation-failure and rollback paths.
